findings.title: Things of the cabin that he sees against a window are drawn as glass or as the outside: at night the arm, what stands on the dash, the shop's upper tray and its price labels (and, on the main line, a passenger) lose four fifths of their light; under the spotlight the dashboard clock is washed out
findings.evidence:
All on 34fc84c under xvfb, pictures in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-I99/1f0e83f4-90ea-55fd-b6c8-8fb38ca9acc1/scratchpad/pfxrev5/.
(1) The game's own command line, `res://scenes/drive.tscn -- --leg=night,2 --bot=line --hud --give=beads,seeds,breath_mints,phone --aim=mirror --shot-frame=300` (night_mirror.png, crop_night_mirror.png): the forearm is rgb 43,31,23 where it crosses the windscreen and 136,93,49 below the dash line; the tops of the things at dash_1 and dash_2 are 26,27,30 over feet of 166,134,36; the beads above the mirror are 31,23,18.
(2) A Telling (drivers, the scene's stand-in driver) run forward to a stop on a Night leg, its save continued with `--continue --hud --aim=offer_8` (night_stop_offer8.png): the snapshot has night true and stopped true, so the dark stays on in the shop. The label 'Arak flask: 45' (upper row, before the passenger's window) has luminance 56, 'Turbo: 0' (before the door) 175; the hand at the upper tray and the vendor are near black.
(3) artifacts/m10_postfx_glare.png (my re-render is pixel-identical): under the motorcade's Glare 80 the dashboard clock stands at 1.45:1 against its ground (18:1 with no effect), on the leg that tests patience against the Clock.
(4) The shader's own arithmetic from his eye (probe_glass.gd): the top of anything 6 cm tall at dash_1 or dash_2, the clock, beads on the mirror, offers 6 to 10, seven of the ten price labels and a passenger's head all lie inside a pane's rectangle. Only what hangs under the Cabin's Mirror and Visor nodes is taken out, and only for the windscreen (planes of constant z).
(5) On the main line (d6094e2, same shader and view) `--leg=night,2 --ride=student --aim=passenger_shoulder` (merged_night_passenger.png): the Student is 28,20,42 above the window sill and 85,56,115 below it.
Milder, same cause: at Haze 0.6 the arm at the visor is veiled, with a seam where the clear strip ends (stage_haze_visor.png); in rain the arm is blurred and rained on and the markers' yellow bleeds into the blurred glass (stage_rain_mirror.png).
GDD 1.3 and 16.3: state is shown by cabin objects (the clock, supplies, beads counted); 16.7: the hand is the most animated thing in the game; 9.6: the hand does the shopping. The builder's decision says the clock and what stands on the dash stay readable: that holds for haze, blur and cracks only. left_undone names the hand at the visor and the mirror ('only slightly paler' under Dawn), not the night, the dash, the clock, the tray or a passenger.
findings.fix: Tell the shader what is cabin, not only where the glass is. Sturdy: draw the Cabin's own visual layer once more into a SubViewport (camera copied, transparent background) and read it in the shader as a mask; where it has alpha the pixel is cabin, whatever stands there. That covers the arm, the dash, the clock, the tray, its labels and a passenger, and the Mirror/Visor rectangles, MAX_BLINDS and the clear strip can go. Smaller but partial: two capsules for the arm, rectangles for what is under ItemMounts, Dash and Stop, planes of constant x for the side windows, MAX_BLINDS raised in the view and the shader alike. Cheapest stopgap for the shop: let the darkness go while the snapshot's `stopped` is true.

findings.title: The cracked windscreen's web covers 3.1% of the picture (13.3% of the windscreen) and lies over the sky and the right shoulder; the GDD says cracks cover 20% of the view
findings.evidence: State `cracks` of tools/post_fx_shots.gd (pixel-identical to artifacts/m10_postfx_cracks.png), measured against the state `none`: the windscreen is 23.2% of the 1920x1080 picture; the disc the shader asks for (line 307, cracks x the pane's area) is 20.0% of the windscreen and 4.6% of the picture, radius 175 px; the cracks drawn reach 141 px on average (the rim of line 254 frays inward by postfx_crack_fray 0.15), so the area inside the outermost cracks is 13.3% of the windscreen and 3.1% of the picture. Its middle is the middle of the glass (postfx_crack_center 0.5, 0.52); his line of sight meets the glass at 0.35 across and 0.28 up, so the web spans x 999..1316, y 284..603 beside the vanishing point at 960,541 and nothing of his own lane is behind it. The same web from a real hit in a real Telling: rain_stop_offer8.png in the scratchpad folder pfxrev5. GDD 5.8 and 6.3: 'Cracks cover 20% of the view'; in the same tables Tunnel's 70% and the Lids' 25% are shares of the picture. The builder reported the reading (20% of the glass) as a decision; even by that reading a third is missing.
findings.fix: Decide and record what 'the view' is here (NEEDS OWNER). As the glass: postfx_crack_fray 0.15 to about 0.05 brings the drawn web to its share, and postfx_crack_center nearer 0.35, 0.28 puts it over the road (data only). As the picture: take the disc's radius from the picture's area instead of the pane's (one line; at 16:9 that is most of the windscreen).

findings.title: Haze at the cap is a veil of 0.45, not 0.60, and the strip above the dash leaves the nearest 12 m of road free of haze, blur and cracks
findings.evidence: State `haze` (uniform haze 0.600, the haze_cap) against `none`, over the sky part of the windscreen: the veil's opacity is 0.451 on average, 0.39 to 0.54; `haze_half` (0.300) gives 0.226. Line 346 multiplies by (1.0 - haze_mottle * thin), which only ever thins (postfx_haze_mottle 0.4). Line 277 besides clears the foot of the glass (postfx_demist_strip 0.05, 0.10): by the eye at y 0.32 and road_y -0.83, the road from 7.9 m to 12.3 m ahead is untouched by haze, rain blur and cracks, and their full strength begins 27.6 m ahead (the report says about 22 m). GDD 5.8: 'The windscreen clouds, up to 60%'; 9.1: 'The view blurs over 6 s without a wiper sweep'. Both readings are reported as decisions; the numbers are mine.
findings.fix: Centre the patches on the snapshot's value, (1.0 + haze_mottle * (0.5 - thin)) clamped to 1, or lower postfx_haze_mottle (data only). The clear strip can go once what stands on the dash is told apart from the glass (finding 1).

findings.title: Tunnel at Nerves 100 leaves more than tunnel_min_view: half the light is still there at 88% of the half-view, and at Nerves 80 the windscreen is untouched
findings.evidence: State `tunnel` (uniform 1.000) against `none`, row y=400: all the light is left out to 73% of the half-view, 71 to 77% of it at 81 to 83%, about 40% at 91%, 9% at the picture's edge. shaders/post_fx.gdshader:388-390 begins the fade at tunnel_min_view (0.7) and ends it at 0.7 + postfx_tunnel_feather (0.35) = 1.05, which is off the picture at mid-height. State `tunnel_half` (Nerves 80): only the far left of the side window and the lower corners darken. GDD 5.8: 'The view narrows to 70% at Nerves 100'; the unit of tunnel_min_view: 'share of the view left at Nerves 100'.
findings.fix: postfx_tunnel_feather 0.35 to about 0.12 (data only), or end the fade at tunnel_min_view instead of beginning it there.

findings.title: At night the ground under the doors is the brightest thing in the picture
findings.evidence: night_stop_offer8.png (scratchpad folder pfxrev5) and the state darkness_right: the ground seen through the 13 cm between each door and the floor (cabin_door is 0.5 m tall at y -0.05, so it ends at -0.30; the floor's top is at -0.43) lies behind no pane, so it takes the cabin's 32% of the night and not the outside's 80%: luminance up to 159 in a picture whose night is under 35. It shows at every far reach to the right or down on a Night leg and at a night stop. Named in left_undone; no fix was proposed.
findings.fix: Close the gap in the data: cabin_door 0.63 m tall in placeholders.json and door_left, door_right at y -0.115 in anchors.json (the top stays at 0.20). The cabin mask of finding 1 would also do it: what is not cabin is outside.

findings.title: glare_position is the one uniform that is neither eased nor held: a light that changes place while its wash is up makes the wash jump every frame
findings.evidence: Headless probe of PostFxView (probe_logic.gd in the scratchpad folder pfxrev5): with glare 0.8 held and `sun` thrown between 0 and 0.6 every frame, glare_position changed 119 times in 2 s with glare_amount at 0.80 (lines 138-143 set `_light` outright; the hold of the last branch covers only a light that has gone out). The amounts do hold: I found at most 6 turns in any second on tunnel, blink, glare_amount and darkness at 30 fps, 144 fps and uneven frame times, and on beam_reach, night_darker and haze_color, which the check tool does not flicker. Today's simulation never has a spotlight and a sun together, so this is not reachable yet; it becomes so with the glare_position key the builder asks of the simulation, or with a second light (GDD 5.8 names high beams). GDD 16.4: 'No effect flashes faster than three times a second'; the view's header says 'whatever the simulation does'.
findings.fix: Move `_light` toward its new place at a rate from tuning instead of setting it, or let it change place only while the eased glare is below a small share; add the case to tools/post_fx_check.gd.

findings.title: The shader keeps look constants as literals, and its header says every number comes from tuning
findings.evidence: Header, line 16: 'Every number comes from data/tuning.json through PostFxView.' Not so: rain_streaks() lines 177-190 (two layers, the second 1.6 times the first, two cells in five hold a streak, 0.25 and 0.5 for its place, 0.35 and 0.65 for its taper); the blur's five taps lines 326-330 (weights 0.36 and 0.16, offsets 1.0 and 0.4, half the radius); the haze's two octaves line 345 (0.65, 0.35, 2.7). docs/CLAUDE.md: 'No tuning literals in code'; the project's other shader, world_bend.gdshader, has none. The view itself is clean (MIN_TIME and MAX_BLINDS are guards, not tuning).
findings.fix: Make uniforms, with tuning names and units, of the ones that shape the look (the share of cells that hold a streak, the second layer's size, the octaves' weights); or say in the header which numbers are the shader's own arithmetic.

findings.title: The two files are not named as GDD 13.2 names them
findings.evidence: GDD 13.2 lists src/view/postfx.gd and shaders/postfx.gdshader, and D-012 reads that list as the required minimum. The branch adds src/view/post_fx_view.gd and shaders/post_fx.gdshader. Reported as a decision by the builder and the integrator; not yet in docs/DECISIONS.md (off limits for their step).
findings.fix: Rename now, while four places refer to them (the preload in the view, the ext_resource in scenes/drive.tscn, SHADER_PATH in tools/post_fx_check.gd, the comments), or record the names in DECISIONS when the entries for this piece are written.

findings.title: Nothing ties the three panes to the cabin they describe, and the check gives the view no camera and no cabin
findings.evidence: postfx_windscreen, postfx_window_left and postfx_window_right are worked out by hand from the props of data/anchors.json and the sizes of data/placeholders.json. I derived them again from the pillars, the dash, the roof and the doors as seen from the eye (0, 0.32, 0.5) and they agree to the millimetre today: -0.636, 0.18, 1.176, 0.675 at z -0.46; -0.305, 0.20, 0.75, 0.653 at x -0.63; -0.352, 0.20, 0.75, 0.684 at x 1.18. In a 2560x1080 window the mask still fits (wide_night_left.png in the scratchpad folder pfxrev5). But tools/post_fx_check.gd sets every view up with setup(_data, null, null) (line 156), so the panes, the blinds and the light's place under a glance are covered by pictures only, and GDD 1.1 lets an artist change the cabin in the registry with no code change: a moved pillar would leave the haze over it with CHECK OK.
findings.fix: About ten lines in tools/post_fx_check.gd: project the edges of the pillars, the dash, the roof and the doors from the eye and compare with the three constants; and one check with a real Camera3D and CabinView that the lowered visor adds a blind (blind_count).

verdict: The branch is fit to merge as it is, as a base, but the post effects are not finished: finding 1 must be fixed before M10's post effects are called done. On 34fc84c tools/check.sh prints CHECK OK (tests 91 of 114 as at 7896556, smoke 0 failures, postfx 166 checks, 0 failures). The rules are kept: nothing under src/core, tests, docs or wip is touched, the shared files carry 3, 4 and 1 lines, the view only reads the snapshot, there is no player-facing text, and both commit messages end as required. What the two reports claim held up: the twelve record pictures and the three leg-driven ones re-render pixel for pixel (darkness_tint differs in 3 pixels and all in 339, as reported), a real Telling showed the Storm with its Night storm, Dawn and the Arrival as the check says, and the flash rule held under every flicker I tried. The branch is already on the main line (b4fbdd2); 8701113 there renamed postfx_sun_position to sun_position and changed nothing else in the view or the shader, so every finding applies there as it stands. What must change first: finding 1, because on Night legs the hand, the shop and a passenger are drawn as if they were outside the car. Finding 2 needs the owner's reading of 'the view'; the other seven are small, mostly one number or one line. Not findings against this branch, because they need src/core: where the light is (the spotlight's lane and the road's bend, the sun's height); what the haze is made of outside the Storm; and high beams as a cause of Glare (GDD 5.8), which DriveSim.glare() does not know. Also to know: check.sh cannot see the shader at all (headless has no renderer and the parse check takes no .gdshader), so a shader that does not compile still gives CHECK OK and the pictures are the only proof; Forward+ and Mobile remain unrun; the post effects check is a step of check.sh, not a registered test; the DECISIONS and PROGRESS entries are still owed. I changed nothing: the worktree is back on its own branch and clean, and my probes and pictures are in the scratchpad folder pfxrev5.
